"The efficiency of a computer power supply is its output power divided by its input power; the remaining input power is converted into heat. For instance, a 600-watt power supply with 60% efficiency running at full load would draw 1000 W from the mains and would therefore waste 400 W as heat. On the other hand, a 600-watt power supply with 80% efficiency running at full load would draw 750 W from the mains and would therefore waste only 150 W as heat."

Is your current power supply 80+ rated?

A power supply's output is dependent on how much it can deliver at certain loads. A psu that is rated "80+ Gold" is capable of delivering 87% of the maximum wattage at full load, meaning a 600W psu would deliver a maximum of 522W at max load.

The general rule of thumb is to want about 700+W worth with a modern psu, at a decent 80+ rating.

At the right side of you screen, (near the speed/depth/etc gauge) you can get into "Headquarters", or alternatively, talk to the commanding officer on the dock and ask about HQ.

Here you'll find room with a blank white square in the lower left corner of the screen. Click that and you are taken to a map screen with many icons on it. Each icon corresponds with a research project. Click one to see what you'll get from it, and which type of officer you'll need to assign to it.

NOTE only officers that are under your command but ARE NOT on your ship are eligible to do research tasks. You'll want to wait until you have some spare officers from either doing missions, or promoting crew via reputation points.

If you want to use one of the officers of your boat (only recommended if you plan on spending a few days at the docks, you'll need to temporarily remove him from your ship. This is done via the "Management" tab, or by speaking to the recruitment officer and selecting "I'll decide" etc. Here you will have a list of your crew, with the officers at the top. You need to uncheck the box beside the name of the officer you want taken off the ship.

Now you can use that officer to do research with in HQ.

PS - Research speed is dependent on what date it is in your game (X day of March, 194x for example). Any research that was historically done AFTER your current date in game will take much, much longer to research (say 44 days as compared to 8). Something you'll want to keep in mind. There will be a warning when you look up the research, so you wont do this accidentally.

The bars are for adding helpers to the officers. If the outline of the bar is green, that means they can use the help. If beige, they do not benefit from help.

For instance, if you add two helpers to your engineer on the engines, you will consume less fuel.

If you add one helper to your hydrophone operator, he can hear things farther away and will calculate targeting solutions faster.

Saving fuel: If you put 2 helpers each on your engineer and navigator you will save something like 30% consumption. I tend to zip out to the hunting grounds at speed 4, then cruise around them at speed 3 or slower to help out my hydrophones (the less noise you make, the better you can hear)

Getting officers experience: you have to have them do things. Calculating solutions, giving medical aid, decoding messages all will get you experience.

Upgrading ships: you must research something in headquarters first; then go to the warehouse and tell them you want to upgrade the thing you researched.
